title: Systems Modeling and Cognitive Audits for Hypercert Ecosystems
description: This document is a grant application to Protocol Labs, from Active Inference Institute (Active Blockference project).  The grant was submitted in October 2022 and was not funded. Learn more, get in touch, get involved, or fund us:  https://www.activeinference.org/

files.name: AII _ Blockference _ Protocol Labs Research RFP.pdf

methods.name: Proposed AEOS specification and Active Blockference models for Hypercerts
methods.description: The proposal plans to build an Active Entity Ontology for Science (AEOS) specification and Active Blockference implementation for Hypercert ecosystems.
methods.evidence: We aim to develop the Hypercert ecosystem towards flexibility, utility, and maturity by creating an AEOS specification, and Active Blockference implementation, for Hypercerts.

methods.name: Planned extension of Active Blockference to multi-agent simulation
methods.description: Plans to expand the currently single-agent Active Blockference simulation into a multi-agent model of Hypercert ecosystems.
methods.evidence: Currently, Active Blockference simulates the cognitive processes and goal-directed behavior of a single-agent. Our goal is to expand this simulation into a multi-agent model

methods.name: Planned informative stakeholder interviews
methods.description: The research strategy begins with interviews with Protocol Labs, Hypercert developers and stakeholders before milestone development.
methods.evidence: We will initially engage in a series of informative interviews with Protocol Labs and Hypercert developers, and stakeholders, to understand the landscape which we will be then developing in.

methods.name: Planned comparative simulations of funding models
methods.description: A milestone deliverable is comparable simulations of traditional, DeSci and Hypercert funding models.
methods.evidence: Compose comparable simulations of traditional, DeSci, and Hypercert funding models that demonstrate advantages and opportunities for improvement for Hypercerts.

key_findings: The proposal identifies limitations in DeSci systems design, including ad hoc flowcharts with informal ontologies and a lack of engineering-grade standards.
It argues agent-based methods are needed to move design from bulk or mean-field approaches to the granularity of single actions by particular entities.
It lays out tentative milestones beginning with entity model construction within 4 months of funding, budgeted at $20,000.
The authors acknowledge a risk that the entity ontology may not yield results favoring the Hypercert mechanism.
key_findings_evidence: Systems are often communicated with ad hoc flowcharts with heterogeneous or partially-specified types of nodes and edges (informal ontologies).
We suggest that agent-based methods are essential to move design considerations from the bulk or mean-field approach, towards the granularity which design & realtime analysis demand
Milestone 1: Entity Model Construction Date: Within 4 months of funding beginning. Budget: $20,000
There is no certainty that the development of an entity ontology for systems using hypercerts will yield results in favor of the hypercert mechanism.
